title: 2 Kings Chapter 7 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Kings chapter 7 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Kings Chapter 7 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Kings Chapter 7.

questions.question: What did Elisha say would be sold for a shekel in the gate of Samaria the next day?
options: A measure of fine flour
A measure of oil
A measure of wine
A measure of honey
questions.correctAnswer: A measure of fine flour
questions.explanation: Elisha said that a measure of fine flour would be sold for a shekel in the gate of Samaria the next day (2 Kings 7:1).

questions.question: What was sold for a shekel along with the measure of fine flour according to Elisha?
options: Two measures of barley
Two measures of wheat
Two measures of olives
Two measures of figs
questions.correctAnswer: Two measures of barley
questions.explanation: Elisha declared that two measures of barley would be sold for a shekel along with the measure of fine flour (2 Kings 7:1).

questions.question: How did the lord whom the king leaned on respond to Elisha's prophecy?
options: He doubted and said it was impossible
He rejoiced and believed fully
He ignored the prophecy
He immediately spread the news
questions.correctAnswer: He doubted and said it was impossible
questions.explanation: The lord expressed disbelief by saying, 'if the LORD would make windows in heaven, might this thing be?' (2 Kings 7:2).

questions.question: What did Elisha say to the lord who doubted the prophecy?
options: He will see it but not eat it
He will neither see nor eat it
He will eat it with joy
He will see and profit
questions.correctAnswer: He will see it but not eat it
questions.explanation: Elisha told the lord he would see the prophecy fulfilled with his eyes but would not eat of it (2 Kings 7:2).

questions.question: Who were sitting at the entering of the gate in 2 Kings 7?
options: Four leprous men
Four prophets
Four soldiers
Four merchants
questions.correctAnswer: Four leprous men
questions.explanation: The text states that four leprous men were sitting at the entering of the gate (2 Kings 7:3).

questions.question: What question did the four leprous men ask one another?
options: "Why sit we here until we die?"
"Where is the king?"
"Shall we enter the city?"
"Who will save us?"
questions.correctAnswer: "Why sit we here until we die?"
questions.explanation: The leprous men asked, 'Why sit we here until we die?' (2 Kings 7:3).

questions.question: What did the leprous men decide to do instead of waiting to die?
options: Go to the Syrian camp hoping to be saved or killed
Enter the city gates immediately
Stay and pray for deliverance
Seek help from Elisha
questions.correctAnswer: Go to the Syrian camp hoping to be saved or killed
questions.explanation: They decided to go to the Syrian camp, reasoning if they were saved they would live, and if killed, they would die (2 Kings 7:4).

questions.question: When did the leprous men rise to go to the camp of the Syrians?
options: In the twilight
At noon
At dawn
In the middle of the night
questions.correctAnswer: In the twilight
questions.explanation: They rose up in the twilight to go to the Syrian camp (2 Kings 7:5).

questions.question: What did the leprous men find when they reached the Syrian camp?
options: There was no man there
The Syrians were preparing for battle
They found the Syrians feasting
The camp was heavily guarded
questions.correctAnswer: There was no man there
questions.explanation: They found the Syrian camp completely empty with no man there (2 Kings 7:5).

questions.question: What caused the Syrians to flee their camp?
options: The LORD made them hear noises of a great host
They were attacked by the Israelites
They ran out of food
They had a sudden illness
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD made them hear noises of a great host
questions.explanation: The LORD caused the Syrians to hear noises of chariots and horses, making them think Israel had hired other kings against them (2 Kings 7:6).

questions.question: What did the Syrians mistakenly believe about the king of Israel?
options: He had hired the kings of the Hittites and Egyptians against them
He was fleeing the city
He was making peace with them
He was surrendering
questions.correctAnswer: He had hired the kings of the Hittites and Egyptians against them
questions.explanation: They thought the king of Israel had hired the kings of the Hittites and Egyptians to come against them (2 Kings 7:6).

questions.question: True or False: The Syrians fled their camp during the day after hearing the noise of a great host.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The Syrians fled in the twilight, not during the day (2 Kings 7:7).

questions.question: True or False: The Syrians left behind their tents, horses, and asses when they fled.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The Syrians left their tents, horses, and asses behind as they fled (2 Kings 7:7).

questions.question: True or False: The lord on whom the king leaned was rewarded for his faith in the prophecy.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The lord was trampled to death by the people at the gate, fulfilling the prophecy that he would see but not eat the good news (2 Kings 7:17).

questions.question: In what order did these events happen in 2 Kings 7? (1) Syrians flee their camp, (2) leprous men decide to go to camp, (3) Elisha prophesies price drop, (4) leprous men find the empty camp
questions.explanation: Elisha prophesied first (v.1), then the leprous men decided to go (v.4), then they found the empty camp (v.5), and the Syrians fled (v.7).

medium.title: 2 Kings Chapter 7 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Kings Chapter 7 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the four leprous men decide to do instead of waiting to die at the city gate?
options: Go to the Syrian camp and risk their lives
Beg for food at the city gate
Pray for deliverance from God
Hide in the city to avoid the famine
questions.correctAnswer: Go to the Syrian camp and risk their lives
questions.explanation: In 2 Kings 7:3-5, the lepers reason that they might as well go to the Syrian camp because if they stay, they will die of famine, but if they go, they might live or die trying.

questions.question: How did the Lord cause the Syrians to abandon their camp?
options: By sending a plague among them
By causing them to hear a noise of a great army
By sending a powerful earthquake
By making them see an angel
questions.correctAnswer: By causing them to hear a noise of a great army
questions.explanation: According to 2 Kings 7:6, the Lord made the Syrians hear the noise of chariots, horses, and a great host, which caused them to flee.

questions.question: What did the lepers do once they found the Syrian camp deserted?
options: They ate, drank, and took silver, gold, and raiment, hiding them
They burned the tents and destroyed the camp
They immediately reported to the king
They waited until morning to leave
questions.correctAnswer: They ate, drank, and took silver, gold, and raiment, hiding them
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 7:8 explains the lepers went into tents, ate and drank, and took valuables which they hid before going to another tent to do the same.

questions.question: Why did the lepers decide to report the empty Syrian camp to the king's household?
options: Because they felt keeping quiet was wrong and feared mischief in the morning
Because they wanted a reward from the king
Because they feared the Syrians would return at night
Because they wanted to return to the city quickly
questions.correctAnswer: Because they felt keeping quiet was wrong and feared mischief in the morning
questions.explanation: In 2 Kings 7:9, the lepers express that it is a day of good tidings and holding their peace was wrong; waiting till morning might bring mischief.

questions.question: What was the initial reaction of the city porter when the lepers told him about the Syrian camp?
options: He called other porters and reported it to the king's house
He doubted the lepers and ignored them
He sent soldiers immediately to investigate
He locked the city gates in fear
questions.correctAnswer: He called other porters and reported it to the king's house
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 7:10-11 describe that the porter called the other porters and they together told the king's household about the empty Syrian camp.

questions.question: How did the king interpret the news about the Syrians' disappearance from their camp?
options: He thought the Syrians were hiding in the fields to ambush them
He believed the Syrians had fled to another city
He assumed the Syrians had been defeated in battle
He thought the Syrians were negotiating peace
questions.correctAnswer: He thought the Syrians were hiding in the fields to ambush them
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 7:12 shows the king's suspicion that the Syrians had hidden themselves in the fields to catch the Israelites as they came out of the city.

questions.question: What practical lesson about faith and obedience can be drawn from the king sending horses to spy on the Syrians after hearing the report?
options: Faith involves testing God’s promises through action
Obedience means waiting passively for deliverance
Doubt should prevent taking any action
Avoid taking risks even when God promises deliverance
questions.correctAnswer: Faith involves testing God’s promises through action
questions.explanation: In 2 Kings 7:13-14, the king heeds the report and sends horses to see for himself, showing that faith includes acting on God's word and seeking confirmation.

questions.question: What did the messengers find on the way to Jordan when they followed the Syrian host?
options: Garments and vessels the Syrians had cast away in haste
A large army waiting to attack Israel
A peaceful Syrian settlement
Empty roads with no signs of the Syrians
questions.correctAnswer: Garments and vessels the Syrians had cast away in haste
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 7:15 reports that the messengers found the road full of garments and vessels abandoned by the fleeing Syrians.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 7:16, what happened after the people learned the Syrians had fled?
options: The people spoiled the tents of the Syrians, and the prices of flour and barley returned to normal
The people decided to rebuild the Syrian camp
The people fled in fear of a possible trap
The people ignored the event and stayed in the city
questions.correctAnswer: The people spoiled the tents of the Syrians, and the prices of flour and barley returned to normal
questions.explanation: After the Syrians fled, the people took their belongings and the famine ended as the prices returned to what the Lord had foretold (2 Kings 7:16).

questions.question: What was the fate of the lord on whom the king leaned, and why?
options: He was trampled to death by the people at the gate
He was promoted to a higher position
He fled the city with the Syrians
He was rewarded for his faith
questions.correctAnswer: He was trampled to death by the people at the gate
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 7:17 and 7:20 explain that this lord was trampled to death by the people in the gate, fulfilling the prophecy made by the man of God.

questions.question: What does the dialogue between the lord and the man of God in verses 2 and 19 teach about belief and skepticism?
options: Skepticism may cause one to witness blessings but miss their benefits
Skepticism is always justified when miracles are predicted
Belief without evidence is foolish
God's promises are conditional on human effort
questions.correctAnswer: Skepticism may cause one to witness blessings but miss their benefits
questions.explanation: The lord doubted the prophecy (2 Kings 7:2,19), and the man of God said he would see it but not eat it, showing skepticism can lead to missing out on blessings.

questions.question: How does 2 Kings 7 teach us about the importance of sharing good news promptly?
options: The lepers recognized the day as good tidings and chose to report it immediately
It is better to wait until full confirmation before sharing news
Good news should be kept secret to avoid jealousy
Only kings should share important news
questions.correctAnswer: The lepers recognized the day as good tidings and chose to report it immediately
questions.explanation: In 2 Kings 7:9-10, the lepers decide not to keep silent about the good news fearing mischief if they delayed, showing the value of prompt proclamation.

questions.question: True or False: The king immediately believed the report that the Syrian camp was deserted and sent his troops out to claim it.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The king initially suspected it was a trap and sent horses to check first, as stated in 2 Kings 7:12-14.

questions.question: True or False: The Lord’s intervention in making the Syrians hear the noise of a great army is an example of divine protection and deliverance.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 7:6 describes how the Lord caused the Syrians to hear a noise of a great army, causing them to flee and thus delivering Israel from siege.

questions.question: True or False: The people’s spoiling of the Syrian tents after their flight indicates a lack of trust in God’s provision.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The spoiling of the tents was a natural consequence of the Syrians’ sudden flight and the end of the famine, fulfilling God's promises as in 2 Kings 7:16.

hard.title: 2 Kings Chapter 7 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Kings Chapter 7.

questions.question: What did the people find along the way as the messengers pursued the Syrians to Jordan?
options: Garments and vessels that the Syrians had cast away in haste
Food supplies left by the Syrians
A hidden Syrian army waiting to ambush them
Nothing but empty land
questions.correctAnswer: Garments and vessels that the Syrians had cast away in haste
questions.explanation: The messengers reported to the king that the way was full of garments and vessels which the Syrians had cast away in their haste, indicating a sudden flight (2 Kings 7:15).

questions.question: What happened to the price of fine flour and barley after the Syrians fled?
options: A measure of fine flour was sold for a shekel and two measures of barley for a shekel
Prices remained high due to scarcity
Barley was more expensive than fine flour
Prices dropped but not according to prophecy
questions.correctAnswer: A measure of fine flour was sold for a shekel and two measures of barley for a shekel
questions.explanation: After the people spoiled the tents of the Syrians, prices returned to normal as prophesied by Elisha, fulfilling the word of the LORD (2 Kings 7:16).

questions.question: Who was appointed by the king to have charge of the gate, and what was his fate?
options: The lord on whose hand the king leaned; he was trodden to death by the people
Elisha; he was honored by the king
A Syrian spy; he was captured
A servant; he escaped unharmed
questions.correctAnswer: The lord on whose hand the king leaned; he was trodden to death by the people
questions.explanation: The king appointed the lord on whose hand he leaned to be in charge of the gate, but the people trod upon him there and he died, in accordance with the prophecy (2 Kings 7:17).

questions.question: Which phrase best expresses the fulfillment of the prophecy given by the man of God about the prices of flour and barley?
options: Two measures of barley for a shekel, and a measure of fine flour for a shekel, shall be to morrow about this time
Prices will never return to normal
Only barley prices will fall
Flour will be scarce but barley abundant
questions.correctAnswer: Two measures of barley for a shekel, and a measure of fine flour for a shekel, shall be to morrow about this time
questions.explanation: The prophecy was fulfilled exactly as spoken by the man of God when the prices dropped to two measures of barley for a shekel and a measure of fine flour for a shekel (2 Kings 7:18).

questions.question: What was the lord’s skeptical response to the prophecy about the prices, and what was the man's reply?
options: He said, 'If the LORD should make windows in heaven, might such a thing be?'; the man replied, 'Thou shalt see it with thine eyes, but shalt not eat thereof.'
He accepted it immediately; the man rejoiced
He ignored the prophecy; the man rebuked him
He asked for signs; the man gave him a sign
questions.correctAnswer: He said, 'If the LORD should make windows in heaven, might such a thing be?'; the man replied, 'Thou shalt see it with thine eyes, but shalt not eat thereof.'
questions.explanation: The lord doubted the prophecy using a vivid metaphor, and the man of God told him he would see the fulfillment but not partake of the benefit, foreshadowing his death (2 Kings 7:19).

questions.question: What happened to the lord on whose hand the king leaned, as prophesied?
options: He was trodden to death by the people at the gate
He was exalted and given riches
He fled the city and escaped
He became king after the current king died
questions.correctAnswer: He was trodden to death by the people at the gate
questions.explanation: The prophecy was fulfilled when the people trampled him at the gate, causing his death, as predicted by the man of God (2 Kings 7:20).

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in the story of the four lepers deciding to go to the Syrians’ camp?
options: Chiasm, highlighting the reversal of fortune
Parable, teaching a moral lesson
Allegory, symbolizing Israel’s faith
Hyperbole, exaggerating the danger
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm, highlighting the reversal of fortune
questions.explanation: The narrative employs chiasm, with the lepers’ decision to risk death leading to unexpected salvation, reflecting a literary reversal typical in prophetic stories (2 Kings 7:3-9).

questions.question: The phrase 'windows in heaven' used by the lord who doubted the prophecy is an example of what kind of biblical imagery?
options: A metaphor expressing impossibility
A simile illustrating hope
A parable teaching faith
A typology of divine judgment
questions.correctAnswer: A metaphor expressing impossibility
questions.explanation: The 'windows in heaven' metaphor conveys the skepticism of an impossible event, highlighting the lord’s doubt about God’s promise (2 Kings 7:2, 19).

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of sudden deliverance from famine as seen in 2 Kings 7?
options: 1 Kings 17, where Elijah is fed by ravens during famine
Genesis 1, creation of the world
Exodus 20, giving of the Ten Commandments
Leviticus 23, festivals of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Kings 17, where Elijah is fed by ravens during famine
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 17 shows God’s provision during famine through Elijah’s experience, paralleling the sudden relief and provision in 2 Kings 7 (2 Kings 7:15-16; 1 Kings 17:4-6).

questions.question: How does the fulfillment of Elisha’s prophecy in 2 Kings 7 relate to the New Testament teaching about faith and witnessing?
options: It exemplifies the fulfillment of God's promises, encouraging believers to trust and testify, as taught in Hebrews 11
It contradicts New Testament teachings on doubt
It shows that prophecy is only for Israel
It is unrelated to New Testament teachings
questions.correctAnswer: It exemplifies the fulfillment of God's promises, encouraging believers to trust and testify, as taught in Hebrews 11
questions.explanation: The fulfillment of prophecy encourages faith and witnessing, aligning with Hebrews 11’s emphasis on faith in God's promises and the certainty of His word (2 Kings 7:16; Hebrews 11:1-2).

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'lord on whose hand the king leaned' in the cultural context of the ancient Near East?
options: He was a trusted advisor or close attendant to the king, symbolizing influence
He was a military general with no real influence
He was a foreign ambassador
He was a religious priest
questions.correctAnswer: He was a trusted advisor or close attendant to the king, symbolizing influence
questions.explanation: In ancient Near Eastern courts, such a lord was a close confidant or advisor, reflecting his high status and influence, as indicated by the king leaning on his hand (2 Kings 7:17).

questions.question: What Hebrew word underlies the term 'measure' used in 2 Kings 7:1 and 7:16, and what is its significance?
options: The Hebrew word is 'seah', a unit of dry measure indicating standard trade quantities
The Hebrew word is 'talent', a unit of weight
The Hebrew word is 'shekel', a monetary unit
The Hebrew word is 'ephah', a large volume measure
questions.correctAnswer: The Hebrew word is 'seah', a unit of dry measure indicating standard trade quantities
questions.explanation: The term 'measure' corresponds to 'seah' in Hebrew, a dry measure used for grains and flour, reflecting the economic and daily life context of the prophecy (2 Kings 7:1,16).

questions.question: True or False: The Syrians fled because they saw a real army of Hittites and Egyptians coming against them.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The Syrians fled because the LORD caused them to hear noises of a great army, making them believe Israel had hired the kings of the Hittites and Egyptians, a divine deception rather than a real army (2 Kings 7:6-7).

questions.question: True or False: The four leprous men initially decided to keep silent about the Syrians’ camp being abandoned because they feared punishment.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The lepers acknowledged that it was a day of good tidings but feared mischief if they delayed, deciding to inform the king’s household, showing initial hesitation (2 Kings 7:9-10).

questions.question: What foreshadowing is present in the man of God's declaration to the lord about seeing but not eating the flour and barley?
options: It foreshadows the lord’s death by trampling, denying him the benefit of the prophecy
It foreshadows a future famine
It foreshadows the destruction of Samaria
It foreshadows Elisha’s own death
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the lord’s death by trampling, denying him the benefit of the prophecy
questions.explanation: The man of God’s words predict that the lord would witness the fulfillment but die before enjoying the prosperity, which occurred when he was trampled at the gate (2 Kings 7:19-20).

theological.title: 2 Kings Chapter 7 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Kings Chapter 7 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated in the LORD's promise that fine flour and barley will be sold cheaply in Samaria the next day?
options: Omnipotence
Immutability
Faithfulness
Wrath
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness
questions.explanation: The LORD's promise that prices will normalize shows His faithfulness to His word, as stated in 2 Kings 7:1. This reliability aligns with God's unchanging nature in fulfilling His promises (Numbers 23:19, Hebrews 10:23).

questions.question: How does the response of the king's lord to Elisha's prophecy in 2 Kings 7:2 reveal human skepticism towards divine intervention?
options: He fully trusts the prophecy
He doubts the possibility of God's intervention
He asks for a sign to confirm the word
He immediately believes and prepares
questions.correctAnswer: He doubts the possibility of God's intervention
questions.explanation: The lord expresses incredulity, questioning if God would 'make windows in heaven' to perform such a miracle, showing human doubt towards God's power (2 Kings 7:2). This reflects common human skepticism about divine action (Psalm 73:11).

questions.question: What theological lesson about human despair and hope can be drawn from the leprous men's decision in 2 Kings 7:3-4?
options: Despair leads to faithlessness
Hope requires taking risks in faith
Isolation is the only safety
Waiting passively ensures survival
questions.correctAnswer: Hope requires taking risks in faith
questions.explanation: The leprous men choose to act despite their desperate situation, reflecting that hope often involves stepping out in faith even when circumstances seem hopeless (2 Kings 7:3-4). This aligns with biblical teaching that faith involves trust and action (Hebrews 11:1).

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 7:6, how did God display His sovereign power over the enemy forces?
options: By sending a plague among them
By making them hear a false noise of a great army
By causing an earthquake
By direct angelic intervention
questions.correctAnswer: By making them hear a false noise of a great army
questions.explanation: God caused the Syrians to hear noises of chariots and horses, making them believe a vast army had come against them, driving them to flee (2 Kings 7:6). This demonstrates God's sovereign control over circumstances (Exodus 14:24-25).

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about God’s providence is taught by the fleeing Syrians leaving all their possessions behind as described in 2 Kings 7:7-8?
options: God neglects earthly affairs
God uses circumstances to fulfill His promises
God punishes the innocent
God is indifferent to material wealth
questions.correctAnswer: God uses circumstances to fulfill His promises
questions.explanation: The Syrians' flight and abandonment of their goods enabled the fulfillment of God's promise to relieve the famine, showing His providential control over events (2 Kings 7:7-8). This aligns with the doctrine of divine providence (Romans 8:28).

questions.question: What does the leprous men's initial silence about their discovery of the empty Syrian camp in 2 Kings 7:9 teach about human response to God's blessings?
options: Silence is always wise
Fear can prevent sharing good news
Selfishness leads to hoarding blessings
Joy should be kept private
questions.correctAnswer: Fear can prevent sharing good news
questions.explanation: The men recognize that keeping silent about the good news is wrong because danger may come if they delay telling others, showing how fear can hinder proclaiming God's blessings (2 Kings 7:9). This relates to biblical encouragement to share testimony (Psalm 66:16).

questions.question: How does 2 Kings 7:12-14 illustrate a biblical principle regarding human assumptions versus God's providential plans?
options: Human assumptions are always correct
God’s plans often contradict human fears
Humans can control all outcomes
God does not intervene in crises
questions.correctAnswer: God’s plans often contradict human fears
questions.explanation: The king assumes the Syrians are hiding to ambush them, but God's providence has caused the Syrians to flee, demonstrating that God's plans can overturn human fears and expectations (2 Kings 7:12-14). Proverbs 19:21 affirms God's sovereign will over human plans.

questions.question: What theological significance does the spoiling of the Syrian tents by the people in 2 Kings 7:16 have in the context of God's judgment and provision?
options: It shows human greed
It illustrates God's judgment on oppressors and provision for His people
It is an example of unjust plundering
It signifies covenant breaking
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates God's judgment on oppressors and provision for His people
questions.explanation: The people taking the Syrians' abandoned goods demonstrates God's judgment on the oppressors and His provision to meet the needs of His people, fulfilling His word (2 Kings 7:16). This aligns with God's justice and mercy (Psalm 72:4).

questions.question: What does the fate of the lord on whom the king leaned, who was trampled to death, teach about divine justice as revealed in 2 Kings 7:17 and 20?
options: God punishes unbelief and scorn even if one witnesses His works
God rewards all who serve the king
Death is random and without meaning
God ignores human sin
questions.correctAnswer: God punishes unbelief and scorn even if one witnesses His works
questions.explanation: The lord who doubted God's promise and mocked it was trampled to death, fulfilling Elisha's prophecy, illustrating that unbelief and scorn toward God's word have consequences even when one sees God's workings (2 Kings 7:17, 20). Hebrews 3:12 warns against hardened unbelief.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the miraculous relief from famine described in 2 Kings 7 is mere coincidence and natural events. What does 2 Kings 7:5-7 actually teach about God's intervention?
options: The events were natural and coincidental
God supernaturally caused the enemy's panic to deliver Israel
The Syrians left because of a strategic decision unrelated to God
The famine ended without divine involvement
questions.correctAnswer: God supernaturally caused the enemy's panic to deliver Israel
questions.explanation: Verses 5-7 show that God caused the Syrians to hear a great army's noise, leading them to flee, illustrating supernatural intervention to save His people, contradicting sceptical naturalistic explanations (2 Kings 7:5-7). This affirms God's providence and sovereignty (Psalm 46:1-3).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight about God's providence and human agency can be drawn from the leprous men’s decision to approach the Syrian camp (2 Kings 7:4-5) and the LORD causing the Syrians to flee (2 Kings 7:6-7)?
options: God's providence nullifies human decisions
Human agency operates independently of divine action
God sovereignly orchestrates circumstances but calls for human faith and action
Human action is futile without immediate divine command
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly orchestrates circumstances but calls for human faith and action
questions.explanation: The lepers chose to act despite danger, while God caused the Syrians to flee, showing a cooperation where human faith and initiative are met by God's sovereign providence (2 Kings 7:4-7). This reflects biblical teaching that God works through human decisions (Philippians 2:12-13).

questions.question: How does the incident of the leprous men hiding the spoils and then deciding to report to the king (2 Kings 7:8-10) reflect on Christian ethics regarding the use of blessings?
options: Blessings should always be kept secret
Selfishness is acceptable in times of crisis
Blessings are to be shared with the community for the common good
One should only use blessings for personal gain
questions.correctAnswer: Blessings are to be shared with the community for the common good
questions.explanation: Initially hiding the spoils, the lepers realize that withholding good news is wrong and decide to share it with the king's household, illustrating that blessings are meant to benefit the wider community (2 Kings 7:8-10). This aligns with biblical teaching on generosity (Acts 20:35).

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 7:18-19 teach about the relationship between divine revelation and human unbelief?
options: Divine revelation always brings immediate faith
Human unbelief can persist even after seeing God’s promises fulfilled
Unbelief prevents God’s promises from coming true
God withholds revelation from skeptics
questions.correctAnswer: Human unbelief can persist even after seeing God’s promises fulfilled
questions.explanation: The lord continued to doubt despite witnessing the fulfillment of the prophecy, indicating that human unbelief can persist even in the face of clear divine revelation (2 Kings 7:18-19). This reflects biblical warnings about hardened hearts (John 12:37-40).

questions.question: How does the narrative of 2 Kings 7 contribute to the broader redemptive story of Scripture concerning God's deliverance of His people?
options: It shows God's indifference to Israel's plight
It highlights God's power to save from oppression and famine
It depicts human strength as the ultimate rescuer
It shows the futility of trusting God
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights God's power to save from oppression and famine
questions.explanation: The chapter narrates God's miraculous deliverance of Israel from Syrian siege and famine, fitting into the biblical theme of God as Redeemer who rescues His people in their distress (2 Kings 7:5-16). This prefigures ultimate redemption in Christ (Isaiah 43:1-3).

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 7:1 combined with 2 Kings 7:16 teach about the certainty of God’s prophetic word and its fulfillment?
options: Prophecies often fail to come true
God’s word is certain and will accomplish His purposes
God changes His mind frequently
Prophecies depend on human effort to be fulfilled
questions.correctAnswer: God’s word is certain and will accomplish His purposes
questions.explanation: The initial prophecy about the prices (7:1) is fulfilled exactly as stated when the people spoil the Syrians' tents (7:16), demonstrating the certainty and reliability of God's prophetic word (Isaiah 55:11).
